text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures end strongly higher as speculation of a sharp increase in German December unemployment data, to be released on Thursday, and strong Treasuries boost sentiment. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.89, up 0.31 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts tread water in an uneventful session, settling slightly higher ahead of U.S. payrolls data on Friday and a raft of domestic data next week. The curve is steepening as investors sell the long end ahead of the monetary meeting next week. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-16/32, up 07/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March PIBOR finishes MATIF business near contract highs amid renewed interest rate cut optimism. Ten-year future hauled up in its wake but caution ahead of U.S. producer price data on Thursday. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.22, up 0.20 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets close slightly firmer in line with German bunds but lacking fresh ideas and any real direction. Operators looking to U.S. data in next two days for impetus. Lira firmer against mark. The March bond future on LIFFE was at 128.14, up 0.41 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries edge up to session highs in late morning trade. Futures market leading rally, as March bond contract holds key support at 111 even and breaks above 100-day average of 111-04. Gains seen limited, with more corporate deals to be priced later. Volume said to be light but heavier than earlier in the week.The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-09/32, up 13/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.77 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bonds end higher as cash bond buying continues from Tuesday, breaking above a resistance level of 124.67 in late trade. A 10-year JGB auction to be held on Thursday may not hurt the market although a record low 2.7 percent coupon is likely. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 124.83, up 0.52 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Another busy day in the new issues market was capped during the afternoon by Mexico's launch of a $1 billion 10-year bond. The deal was indicated 337.5 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. Earlier headlines were grabbed by the European Investment Bank's 500 million sterling ($844 million) 10-year bond as the pound remained in vogue. The mark saw its first serious activity of the year. The lira also figured among the more than 30 mainstream deals launched during the day.
